title_en: Regulations on Prevention and Control of Pneumoconiosis of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: These Regulations are formulated to protect the health of workers, eliminate dust hazards, prevent the occurrence of pneumoconiosis, and promote the development of production.
These Regulations shall apply to all enterprises and institutions with dust operations.
Pneumoconiosis refers to a disease mainly characterized by pulmonary fibrosis resulting from the inhalation of dust during production activities.

Local people's governments at all levels shall strengthen leadership over the prevention and treatment of pneumoconiosis. In formulating the local plans for national economic and social development, they shall make overall arrangements for the prevention and treatment of pneumoconiosis.

The competent departments of enterprises and institutions shall, in accordance with the national health and other relevant standards and in light of the actual conditions, formulate plans for the prevention and treatment of pneumoconiosis of enterprises under their jurisdiction, and supervise their implementation.
The competent departments of township enterprises must designate specialized personnel to be responsible for the prevention and treatment of pneumoconiosis in township enterprises, establish a supervision and inspection system, and guide the township enterprises in the prevention and treatment of pneumoconiosis.

The persons in charge of enterprises and institutions shall bear direct responsibility for the prevention and treatment of pneumoconiosis in their units, and shall take effective measures to ensure that the dust operation sites in their units meet the national health standards.

All enterprises and institutions with dust operations shall adopt comprehensive dust prevention measures and new technologies, new processes, and new equipment that are dust-free or low-dust, so that the dust concentration at the operation sites does not exceed the national health standards.

The diagnostic criteria for pneumoconiosis shall be formulated by the administrative department of health, and the health standards for dust concentration shall be jointly formulated by the administrative department of health together with the labor and other relevant departments.

The system for appraisal and finalization of dust prevention facilities shall be formulated by the labor department in conjunction with the administrative department of health. Except under special circumstances, no enterprise or institution shall, without the approval of the competent higher authority, stop the operation or dismantle the dust prevention facilities.
The funds for dust prevention shall be included in the plan for capital construction and technical renovation funds, used for specific purposes, and shall not be misappropriated.

It is strictly prohibited for any enterprise or institution to transfer, subcontract, or in the form of joint operation, assign dust operations to township or street enterprises or individual industrial and commercial households without dust prevention facilities.
All kinds of school-run practice factories or workshops in primary and secondary schools are prohibited from engaging in dust operations.

The protective equipment used by workers to prevent dust hazards must comply with the relevant national standards. Enterprises and institutions shall establish strict management systems and educate workers to use such equipment in accordance with the provisions and requirements.
For workers who engage in dust operations for the first time, the unit they work for shall provide education on dust prevention knowledge and conduct an examination; only after passing the examination may they engage in dust operations.
Minors under the age of 18 are prohibited from engaging in dust operations.

For newly constructed, reconstructed, expanded, or continued construction projects with dust operations, the dust prevention facilities must be designed, constructed, and put into operation simultaneously with the main project. The design task document must be reviewed and approved by the local administrative department of health, the labor department, and the trade union organization before construction may commence. For completion acceptance, the local administrative department of health, the labor department, and the trade union organization shall participate; if the requirements are not met, the project shall not be put into operation.

When the dust concentration at the operation site exceeds the national health standards, no active control measures are taken, and the safety and health of workers are seriously affected, workers shall have the right to refuse to operate.

The administrative department of health, the labor department, and the trade union organization shall divide their work, cooperate, and supervise the prevention and treatment of pneumoconiosis in enterprises and institutions.

The administrative department of health shall be responsible for the monitoring of health standards; the labor department shall be responsible for the monitoring of labor health engineering and technical standards.
The trade union organization shall be responsible for organizing the workers to supervise the prevention and treatment of pneumoconiosis in their units, and for educating workers to comply with the operating procedures and dust prevention systems.

All enterprises and institutions with dust operations must regularly measure the dust concentration at the operation sites. The measurement results must be reported to the competent department and the local administrative department of health, the labor department, and the trade union organization, and be published to workers on a regular basis.
Units engaged in dust operations must establish archives of dust measurement data.

The administrative department of health and the labor department shall strengthen professional guidance to the dust measurement institutions of enterprises and institutions engaged in dust operations, and shall strengthen professional guidance and technical training to the dust measurement personnel.

All enterprises and institutions must conduct health examinations for workers newly engaged in dust operations. For workers who are currently or have formerly been engaged in dust operations, regular health examinations must be conducted. The contents, time limits, and diagnostic criteria for pneumoconiosis shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of the administrative department of health on occupational disease management.

All enterprises and institutions must implement the occupational disease reporting system, and report on the incidence and deaths from pneumoconiosis among workers to the local administrative department of health, the labor department, the trade union organization, and the competent department of their units within the prescribed time limit.

All enterprises and institutions, for workers who have been definitively diagnosed with pneumoconiosis, must transfer them from dust operation posts and provide them with treatment or convalescence. The social insurance benefits for pneumoconiosis patients shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State.
Units and individuals that have made outstanding achievements in the prevention and treatment of pneumoconiosis shall be rewarded by their competent higher authorities.

If a party disagrees with the penalty, it may, within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the penalty notice, apply to the higher authority of the department that made the decision for reconsideration. However, the decision to suspend operations for rectification shall be executed immediately. The higher authority shall make a reply within thirty days from the date of receipt of the application. If the party disagrees with the reply, it may file a prosecution with the People's Court within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the reply.

If the persons in charge of enterprises and institutions, or the supervision and monitoring personnel, neglect their duties, causing losses to public property, the State, and the interests of the people, where the circumstances are minor, they shall be given administrative sanctions by their competent departments; where major losses are caused and a crime is constituted, the judicial organs shall, according to law, pursue the criminal liability of the persons directly responsible.
These Regulations shall be jointly interpreted by the administrative department of health and the labor department of the State Council.

The people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall, in light of local actual conditions, formulate implementing measures for these Regulations.
These Regulations shall come into force as of the date of promulgation.
